panels.description: Reads the `version` label of `switchyard_build_info`. The sample value is the constant 1 - a presence marker, never a version string - so the panel displays the label instead of the value. Scrape freshness is the SCRAPE AGE panel beside it. Current release is shown in panel 12007.
panels.title: BUILD VERSION

panels.description: `up` for the Switchyard scrape target. 0=red (down), 1=green (up), no-series=neutral. This is target reachability, not provider availability.
panels.title: SCRAPE TARGET UP

panels.description: Seconds since the latest `switchyard_build_info` sample was scraped. Green <300s, orange 300-900s, red >900s, absent=neutral. This is the age of the latest build-info sample, not proof every provider is healthy.
panels.title: SCRAPE AGE

panels.description: In-flight algorithm count (gauge). Green at normal concurrency, orange warning (20), red high (50). Thresholds are not proven service capacity.
panels.title: ALGORITHMS IN FLIGHT

panels.description: Client non-ok rate over 5m (includes disconnects). Green <5%, orange 5-20%, red >20%, no-series=neutral. Numerator/denominator unchanged. 91007 supplies idle distinction. The clamp caveat: rate is clamped to [0,1] when denominator is zero.
panels.title: CLIENT NON-OK RATE (5m)

panels.description: Count of distinct model labels with >0 requests in 5m. Neutral color including zero; no red for zero or green for mere activity. Uses sum of per-model boolean > bool 0 if series exist; no artificial zero if no series.
panels.title: ACTIVE REQUEST MODEL LABELS (5m)

panels.description: Process request counter (instant). Neutral blue/text. No lifetime/spend claim.
panels.title: PROCESS REQUESTS

panels.description: 24h all-model request count (instant). Neutral numeric including zero; no red for idle.
panels.title: REQUEST ATTEMPTS - ALL MODELS (24h)

panels.description: Non-ok upstream attempts (24h). 0=green, 1=orange, 20=red, missing=neutral. These are upstream attempts, not client failures.
panels.title: UPSTREAM NON-OK (24h)

panels.description: HTTP 429 upstream count (24h). 0=green, 1=orange, 20=red, missing=neutral. 429 may be throttling or daily allowance; not HTTP status alone.
panels.title: UPSTREAM 429s (24h)

panels.description: Process error counter (historical, since process start). Neutral; not current health. Resets on restart.
panels.title: TOTAL ERRORS (SINCE PROCESS START)

panels.description: Count of model series that exist (instant). Neutral including zero; no service health or route census claim.
panels.title: MODEL SERIES THAT EXIST (not advertised census)

panels.description: Responses in 5m (extrapolated). Neutral; explicit missing vs zero; no rounding claim exact.
panels.title: RESPONSES (5m)

panels.description: Genuine error share (5m): numerator excludes client_disconnected, denominator includes disconnects. Green/orange/red percentage; NaN/idle/missing neutral. If error series absent while denominator positive, distinguishes proven no errors from absent telemetry; does not silently change denominator or inject unconditional zeros.
panels.title: CLIENT ERROR SHARE (5m, excludes disconnects from numerator)

panels.description: Traffic state (5m): zero→IDLE grey, positive→traffic neutral (not green implying success), absent→NO SERIES grey, query error distinct. Companion to panel 12.
panels.title: TRAFFIC STATE (5m)

panels.description: Google-family model activity by heuristic (selected_model=~gemini-.+|gemma-…), not owner account. A=calls(1h) neutral, B=ok(24h) green, C=error(24h) red, D=latest counter scrape age in seconds (dateTimeFromNow). Model-family heuristic, not owner account.
panels.title: GOOGLE MODEL ACTIVITY (model-family attribution, not account)

panels.description: Client response counts in 5m by outcome (extrapolated increase()). A=ok green, B=retryable_error orange, C=other_error red, D=client_disconnected grey. Neutral fixed default. Shared min0 scale. No fabricated zero. Counts are extrapolated increase().
panels.title: CLIENT OUTCOMES (5m) - COUNTS BY OUTCOME

panels.description: 15-minute rolling response counts by outcome (stacked bars, one count axis, no total/percentages). Neutral fixed default, byName semantic colors. Panel 12 is a KPI, not a percentage trend; the 5m ratio is in 91006.
panels.title: CLIENT OUTCOMES (15m rolling counts)

panels.description: Request rate grouped into model families by the native `model` label. Families are heuristic and mutually exclusive; an `unclassified` series carries traffic matching no named family so the sum reconciles to all-model traffic. Legends name the family only: a shared native model id cannot be attributed to an owner vs Stephen credential from this metric. Unit requests/s.
panels.title: MODEL-FAMILY TRAFFIC (native model labels, heuristic)

panels.description: Incoming request rate by the raw `model` metric label (caller label, not selected model or account).
panels.title: INCOMING MODEL REQUEST RATE

panels.description: LLM call rate by `selected_model` physical label. No successful-completion or account claim.
panels.title: LLM CALLS BY SELECTED MODEL

panels.description: Call rate by routing algorithm (identity palette). Scope matches panels 16/17 algorithm filter.
panels.title: CALLS BY ALGORITHM

panels.description: Decision rate by algorithm and selected_model. Existing algorithm filter.
panels.title: DECISIONS BY ALGORITHM / SELECTED MODEL

panels.description: Estimated decisions in 24h by algorithm and selected_model. Columns Algorithm / Selected model / Estimated decisions (24h), numeric descending sort.
panels.title: DECISION TOTALS (24h)

panels.description: Estimated requests in 24h by incoming model. One row per model, numeric descending sort. No model-to-cost inference.
panels.title: REQUESTS BY MODEL (24h)

panels.description: Upstream attempt rate by outcome and HTTP code. Legend `{{outcome}} · {{code}}`. Neutral fixed default; anchored byRegexp: ^ok green, ^error/^other_error red, ^retryable_error orange, ^client_disconnected grey. Unit attempts/s. Status not inferred from HTTP code alone.
panels.title: UPSTREAM ATTEMPTS BY OUTCOME / CODE

panels.description: Error rate by model (errors/s). Identity palette (all are error counts, no status semantics).
panels.title: ERRORS BY MODEL

panels.description: Client response rate by outcome. Legend `{{outcome}}`. Neutral fixed default; exact byName: ok green, retryable_error orange, other_error red, client_disconnected grey. Unit responses/s.
panels.title: CLIENT RESPONSES BY OUTCOME

panels.description: LLM call rate by outcome. Legend `{{outcome}}`. ok green, error red, neutral unknown. Unit calls/s.
panels.title: LLM CALL RATE BY OUTCOME

panels.description: Run termination rate by outcome. Legend `{{outcome}}`. ok/success green, error/failure red, retryable orange, disconnected/cancelled grey, unknown neutral. Unit runs/s (not request count).
panels.title: RUN TERMINATIONS BY OUTCOME

panels.description: Recovered retries in rolling 24h (count, not rate). Fixed green for actual recovery. Multiple scrape labels preserved.
panels.title: RECOVERED RETRIES (rolling 24h)

panels.description: Estimated upstream attempts in 24h by HTTP code and outcome. Instant table: columns HTTP code / Outcome / Estimated attempts (24h), count descending. The Outcome cell is coloured per value; a 429 may be a daily allowance or a throttle.
panels.title: UPSTREAM HTTP CODES (code / outcome, 24h)

panels.description: Model-call latency quantiles over 5m rolling histogram estimate. A p50, B p95, C p99. Unit ms. No nonexistent quantile label.
panels.title: MODEL-CALL LATENCY p50 / p95 / p99

panels.description: Total latency p95 by model (includes provider-call + routing overhead). Legend `{{model}} p95`. Unit ms.
panels.title: TOTAL LATENCY p95 BY MODEL

panels.description: Routing overhead p95 by algorithm (identity palette). Unit ms.
panels.title: ROUTING OVERHEAD p95

panels.description: LLM call duration p95 by outcome (5m rolling histogram). Legend `{{outcome}}`. ok green, error red, neutral default. Unit ms. No arbitrary 10s axis cap; plateaus may be histogram bucket limit (inspect le buckets/+Inf).
panels.title: LLM CALL DURATION p95 BY OUTCOME

panels.description: Run duration p95 by outcome (5m rolling histogram). Legend `{{outcome}}`. Same semantic mappings as panel 34. Unit ms. No smoothing null gaps or arbitrary caps.
panels.title: RUN DURATION p95 BY OUTCOME

panels.description: Model-call latency quantiles over 7d (instant). Three instant quantile queries joined by model. Columns p50/p95/p99 (ms), numeric p95 desc, preserve missing. Explicit Prometheus DS.
panels.title: MODEL-CALL LATENCY (7d) - p50 / p95 / p99

panels.description: Token rate by component: A=prompt, B=completion, C=reasoning. Unit tokens/s. No cached/cache_creation claim. Identity colors distinguish components; no summing potentially overlapping counts.
panels.title: TOKEN RATE BY COMPONENT (prompt / completion / reasoning)

panels.description: prompt tokens by model. Legend `{{model}}`. Unit tokens/s.
panels.title: PROMPT TOKENS BY MODEL

panels.description: completion tokens by model. Legend `{{model}}`. Unit tokens/s.
panels.title: COMPLETION TOKENS BY MODEL

panels.description: reasoning tokens by model. Legend `{{model}}`. Unit tokens/s.
panels.title: REASONING TOKENS BY MODEL

panels.description: Cache hit share = cached_tokens / (prompt_tokens > 0). Denominator P=sum by(model)(rate(prompt_tokens_total[5m])); numerator C=same cached_tokens_total. Uses C/(P>0) so idle denominator is absent, not fabricated zero. Legend `{{model}}`. Provider accounting semantics verified; if cached not subset of prompt, limitation labeled.
panels.title: CACHE HIT SHARE

panels.description: Cached token rate by model. Legend `{{model}}`. Unit tokens/s.
panels.title: CACHE TOKEN RATE (tokens/s)

panels.description: Estimated cascade events in 24h. Instant table: Parent / Child / Outcome / Estimated events (24h), numeric desc, no duplicate Time. Outcome value colors: attempt_failed red, skipped_ineligible neutral/orange, selected neutral. No retired ST_RouteFree text; historical data retained. Query does not group capability.
panels.title: CASCADE CHILD OUTCOMES (24h)

panels.description: Cascade crossings by parent/reason (rolling 5m, count). Legend `{{parent_route}}: {{reason}}`. Crossings not errors; neutral default, orange known temporary capacity, red actual failure. No stale invented reason taxonomy.
panels.title: CASCADE CROSSINGS (rolling 5m)

panels.description: Cascade skips (A) and failures (B) in 24h by capability. Legend `skipped · {{parent_route}} · {{capability}}` / `failed · ...`. Colors by refId: grey/orange skips, red failure. Capability is not complete reason taxonomy.
panels.title: CASCADE SKIPS & FAILURES (rolling 24h, capability label)

panels.description: Stephen cascade child outcomes in 24h (parent_route=ST_Route). Legend is the compound `child_route · outcome`; colour is applied by anchored byRegexp on that compound legend.
panels.title: STEPHEN CASCADE CHILD OUTCOMES (rolling 24h)

panels.description: Stephen cascade selections in 24h by child_route,target. Legend `{{child_route}} → {{target}}`. Selection is not serving unless proven by emitter; neutral identity colors. No invented served counter.
panels.title: STEPHEN CASCADE SELECTIONS (rolling 24h)

panels.description: Purchased credit and remaining balance by provider/currency (gauges, not spend). Current queries aggregate provider,currency; authoritative account label absent, so account-level split unavailable. Columns Provider / Currency / Purchased credit / Remaining balance. Preserve missing and currency; no unsafe sums.
panels.title: PROVIDER CREDIT & BALANCE (account attribution unavailable)

options.content:
**MASTER DIRECT ROUTES — every defined direct alias, 55 of 55, all advertised, none held.** Read from the deployed manifest (`routes.toml` sha256 `a7ef91747befd072…`, 133,545 B, release `20261128T034335Z-6a8209f97101563b-a7ef9174`), `/v1/models` read at 74 of 74 advertised on the service listener (2026-11-28T03:44Z), and — for the documented-capability columns — a join taken 2026-11-25 against the OpenRouter listing, the ThaiLLM listing, the HTPC serving front's own `/v1/models` and `/props`, and the owner's five-target model-card record (issue-35 comment 7119022628). Row 50 is new since the previous revision: `direct-openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` was admitted by release `20261127T091816Z-aaf1bec88835acac-c635222b`, so rows 50-55 were renumbered and the table is no longer '54 of 54'.

Three planes, kept apart on purpose. **Model input / output / doc tools** are what the vendor documents for the model, not what this deployment has carried. **SW t/v/vid** is what the Switchyard *route* declares from this manifest; a declaration is an admission gate — it never proves the vendor supports the modality, and it never proves the wire carries it. **Transport** is the wire family's status: `cfg` configured but unproven, `ex` an official provider example exists, `?` unknown.

> A route whose declared vision is `N` is **not** evidence that the model cannot see images. It means that route has never admitted one. Gemini 3 Flash/3.1/3.5/3.6 document image, audio, video and PDF input; the owner and Stephen routes both currently declare `vision=false` because the carrier was never qualified, which is a Switchyard statement, not a Google one.

**Input letters** t text · i image · a audio · v video · p pdf, each `✓` documented, `~` partial/example only, `cfg` id live but modalities undocumented, `?` no cited source, `NO` documented unsupported, `—` not an API modality. **Transport** `chat:obs` means this deployment has served that model id in the retained routing log (2026-11-21T00:55Z..2026-11-25T15:08Z); `chat:cfg` means declared and loadable, never seen serving. A model id shared by two targets cannot be attributed to one of them from the log alone. `?` means no cited source establishes the fact (the reason is named in the Evidence column); it is not a negative claim — it is not a negative.

**Evidence join of this revision (2026-11-25).** Every cell that previously read `NOT ASSESSED` was revisited: 79 are now established from a named source, 32 remain unknown with the reason recorded in the Evidence column, across 37 rows. No cell was promoted to a documented claim on the strength of the manifest's own declaration; the `SW t/v/vid` column remains the Switchyard declaration, which is an admission gate and not a capability proof.

**Local fronts.** `Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_0` and `Qwen3.5-9B-MTP` are owner-hosted with no vendor card. Their 81,920 is read from the serving front itself — `/v1/models` `context_length` and `/props` `n_ctx`, both 81,920 on 2026-11-25 — so the number is the target's real capacity and not a borrowed route context. The `smartlocal` and `smartlocal-nt` routes advertise 152,832; that is the escalation leg's R2 declaration and, because a passthrough performs no admission check against it, it is never a guarantee for the HTPC leg, which escalates at 61,440 estimated input.


**Account split.** OpenRouter 13 · Stephen OpenRouter 9 · Owner Google 8 · Stephen Google 8 · thaillm 5 · htpc 3 · comfyninja 2 · deepseek 2 · openai 2 · deepseek_nt 1 · openai_nt 1. The two Google credential groups bill different keys: `SWITCHYARD_GEMINI_API_KEY` for the `direct-google-*` leaves and `SWITCHYARD_GEMINI_STEPHEN_API_KEY` for the `direct-google-stephen-*` leaves. Same model facts, separate money and separate free-tier quota.

**Deployment delta and row-set delta of this revision.** The panel previously described the manifest read at 2026-11-24 (`21f7d771…`, release `20261124T063451Z-c475f2410ba55580-21f7d771`), which is no longer retained on the host. The rows are now enumerated from `e887392c…` (132,140 B, release `20261127T045138Z-fb12d2881387e338-2a20067b`) and reconciled against `/v1/models`: **53 rows became 54**, the addition being `direct-openrouter-tencent-hy4-flash` (`tencent/hy4-flash`, 1,048,576 ctx, input text+image, tools and reasoning in `supported_parameters`, all read from the OpenRouter listing on 2026-11-27). It is `chat:cfg` rather than `chat:obs` because no call has been made through this route, so no wire observation exists for it. No row was removed and no route was renamed. The `SW t/v/vid` column stays a Switchyard declaration — an admission gate, never a vendor capability proof.


**One row changed reach, not definition (2026-11-27).** `direct-deepseek-deepseek-v4-pro` is defined, advertised and unchanged. What changed is narrower than its own route: `deepseek-v4-pro` was removed from `smart-route` on every path — group membership, candidate order and fallback — so that one lane no longer reaches it. Deliberate-use and legacy paths are untouched. The direct alias `direct-openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` is installed and advertised; on 2026-11-28 it was removed from `smart-route` automatic dispatch and kept as a manual direct route.

**Ultra is admitted, and the earlier 'held' wording was wrong (corrected 2026-11-28).** `direct-openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` and its target `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` are installed and advertised; on 2026-11-28 the route was removed from automatic dispatch (group membership cleared, deleted from `smart-route` candidates), so `smart-route` is now 11 = 5/3/1/2. Admission is not the same as being attempted: the 2026-11-27T22:39:38Z and 22:39:46Z decision records show Ultra in the 11-candidate dispatch order and no attempt against it, because a preceding sibling in the same free group (`ling-3.2-flash:free`) had already returned `provider_allowance_exhausted` and the shared allowance was therefore blocked. Neither the panel nor the release notes should describe that as 'held' or 'not installed'.

panels.title: MASTER DIRECT ROUTES - 55 ALIASES (ONE TABLE, ALL DEFINED)

options.content: **ROUTING TOPOLOGY — 19 advertised non-direct routes, 1 non-advertised chat composite (`ST_Route`), 4 typed-decision lanes and 1 decision composition (`smart-decision`).** Regenerated from the deployed manifest (`routes.toml` sha256 `a7ef91747befd072…`, 133,545 B, release `20261128T034335Z-6a8209f97101563b-a7ef9174`) and cross-checked against `/v1/models` on the service listener (127.0.0.1:4000, **74 of 74 advertised**, 2026-11-28). `smart-route` is `selection = grouped` over four ordered pool groups totalling **9 leaves = 3/3/1/2**: `smart-gemini-chat` (3), `smart-openrouter-free` (3: `openrouter-ernie-5_5-flash-preview-free` → `openrouter-ling-3_2-flash-free` → `openrouter-nemotron-3_5-super-vl-free`), `smart-deepseek-flash` (1: `deepseek-deepseek-flash`), and `smart-openrouter-paid` (2: `openrouter-tencent-hy4-flash` → `openrouter-glm-5_3-flash`). `openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` was removed from automatic dispatch on 2026-11-28 (its group membership was cleared and it was removed from `smart-route` candidates); its direct alias `direct-openrouter-nemotron-3-ultra-free` is preserved for manual use. On 2026-11-28 the two Google Gemini Lite leaves (`direct-google-gemini-3.5-flash-lite` and `direct-google-gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) were withdrawn from the same ladder: their `groups` lost `smart-gemini-chat` and each was removed from the route's `candidates`, while their `smart-gemini-bounded` membership and both direct aliases were preserved. The Gemini chat pool is therefore `direct-google-gemini-4-hydrogen` → `direct-google-gemini-3.8-flash` → `direct-google-gemini-3.6-flash`. `deepseek-deepseek-v4-pro` is excluded from `smart-route` on every path; its direct alias is retained. The single chat composite is `ST_Route` (children `ST_Free`, `ST_Paid`; not advertised). The decision composition is `smart-decision` (`capability_first`) over the four typed lanes `smart-gemini-decision` (reconciled from the retired `google-decision`), `smartlocal-decision`, `smartfree-decision`, `ST_Decisions`, served at `/v1/decisions` rather than `/v1/chat/completions`. A declared route context is an advertisement, not an admission check.

**TYPED OPERATIONS — decisions / embed / rerank (separate from the 74 chat routes).**

| Capability | Target | Format | Declared limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smart-decision` (composition) | children: `smart-gemini-decision`, `smartlocal-decision`, `smartfree-decision` | capability_first | declared order |
| `smart-gemini-decision` | direct-google-gemini-decision-1 | google decisions | /v1beta/decisions |
| `smartlocal-decision` | jev-style / laya (HTPC) | typed | /v1/systemone |
| `smartfree-decision` | span-01-lite (Owner OR) | typed | /api/alpha/decisions |
| `ST_Decisions` | span-01-lite (Stephen OR) | typed | /v1/decisions |

**Embedding / reranking contracts:**

| Capability | Target | Format | Declared limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `smartlocal-embedding` | embedding-local | embeddings | 1024D · L2 · batch 64 |
| `smartfree-embedding` | embedding-free-nemotron | embeddings | 4096D · L2 · batch 64 |
| `ST_Embed` | embedding-stephen | embeddings | 4096D · L2 · batch 64 |
| `smartlocal-rerank` | reranker-local | Jina/Cohere | max 64 candidates · top 64 |
| `smartfree-rerank` | reranker-free | Jina/Cohere | max 64 candidates · top 64 |
| `ST_Rerank` | reranker-stephen | Jina/Cohere | max 64 candidates · top 64 |

**5 physical decision targets:** Gemini Decision 1, JEV Style, Laya, owner SPAN-01 Lite, Stephen SPAN-01 Lite. Owner and Stephen credentials are never pooled.

**CREDENTIAL AND REGISTRY BOUNDARIES — refreshed against release `20261128T034335Z-6a8209f97101563b-a7ef9174` (`routes.toml` sha256 `a7ef91747befd072…`, 133,545 B; 2026-11-28).** Keys are referenced by scope, never shown. Separate owner and Stephen credentials cannot be pooled.

| Identity / credential scope | Distinction |
|---|---|
| Owner OpenRouter vs Stephen OpenRouter | Different credentials and billing histories, even for identical native model strings |
| Owner Google vs Stephen Google | separate keys, separate free-tier quota, same model facts |
| DeepSeek vs DeepSeek-NT | Same provider account, different reasoning policy |
| OpenAI vs OpenAI-NT | Codex OAuth, not a raw API key |
| HTPC / ComfyNinja | Owner-operated hardware; compute not free in absolute terms |
| ThaiLLM | Independent upstream credential |

**Registry census (2026-11-28):** 74 advertised chat routes on `/v1/models` — 55 direct aliases (5 owner-operated local: 2 ComfyNinja, 3 HTPC) and 19 non-direct (1 non-advertised chat composite `ST_Route`, 1 decision composition `smart-decision`, 4 typed-decision lanes, embedding and reranking lanes). The Turnstone model registry is a separate surface and is not identical to the Switchyard route count by definition.

**DATED CARRIER TEST MATRIX — not a live capability monitor.** 200/2xx means accepted; 404 carrier refusal; 402 billing gate; 429 inconclusive. Never represent a failed probe as a missing feature.

| Tested target (credential) | Text | Image inline | Image URL | Video inline | Video URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stephen GLM | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 (4.2s) | **200 (39.8s)** |
| Stephen Nemotron | 200 | 200 | 404 | 200 (5.5s) | 404 |
| Owner OR Nemotron | 200 | 200 | 404 | 402 | 404 |
| Owner OR ERNIE | 200 | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Owner OR Ling | 200 | 429 | ? | n/a | n/a |
| DeepSeek Flash NT | 200 | 200 | n/a | n/a | n/a |
| Owner OR Gemma 26B | 429 | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Owner OR Gemma 31B | 429 | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Stephen OR Gemma 26B | 429 | ? | ? | ? | ? |
| Stephen OR Gemma 31B | 429 | ? | ? | ? | ? |

**Important source contradiction resolved:** V7.57 included a blanket statement that no remote video succeeded, while its measured Stephen GLM row records **remote video 200** on Nov 11. The blanket statement is false for that credential/target and must not be repeated. Owner OR Nemotron's 402 is a separate account billing gate, **not** global evidence of unsupported remote video.

**Other dated probes:** Nov16 Ling 17.5s thinking-on vs 1.4s NT (same prompt); `smartfree` ~250K input served by Nemotron in 50.7s. DeepSeek Flash NT tools, JSON, streaming and reasoning=none succeeded; Luna baseline encountered 429. Four decision targets returned 200 on Nov11; score validity separate from transport. Full historical probe detail is retained in the read-only archived V7.57 text inventory and Issue #35 evidence, not scattered among live charts.

**OPERATIONAL INTERPRETATION & SAFETY.** Charts above are measurements; this section explains their boundaries.

- **Health:** `UP=1` means Prometheus target scrape, not that every provider is callable. Build-info gauge value `1` does not itself display the binary version. Live release is in the dated release panel below.
- **Model identity:** `upstream_model` is readable vendor/source identity; exact native `api_model_id` is preserved in the master table. Identical model IDs may be served under different credential scopes. Derived model-family traffic cannot prove billed provider or owner-vs-Stephen usage when model labels overlap.
- **Context/vision:** advertised windows do not guarantee large-input admission on passthrough. `smartlocal*` advertise 152,832 through ComfyNinja VL but R2 residency was unproven. No claims of local GPU readiness from chat metrics.
- **Rate limits:** account-wide OpenRouter free daily allowance is **not** per-model quota. The shipped free-cap classifier recognized `free-models-per-day` even without metadata. Per-minute 429 is distinct.
- **Cost:** purchased provider credit and remaining provider balance are account gauges. Per-request spending, user-level cost and the model quality optimizer are **NOT instrumented/proven**. No composite is a cost/quality judge.
- **Registry visibility:** four aliases are defined and callable but omitted from `offered_aliases` because a utility role names them — `smart-nt` (`perception.model_alias`), `smart-judge` (`judge.model`), `smart-decision` (`judge.output_guard_model`), `smartfree-rerank` (`tools.reranker_alias`); `model.task_alias` also names `smart-nt` but hides nothing. Registered `context_window` is an admission bound, not usable input: `ctx − min(max_tokens, ctx/4) − 5%` yields 244,941 at 262,144 with `max_tokens` 4096 and 216,269 at the 32,768 default, and the session auto-compacts at 80% of the window.
- **No data:** measured zero, absent series and datasource query error are different. `switchyard_composition_*` is lazily emitted by real routing events. Missing data from panels 17, 10506 or 9107 must be inspected but cannot be replaced with fabricated zeros.
- **Transport:** `/responses` video input uses `{"type":"input_video","video_url":"https://... or data:..."}`. `openai_nt` uses the same Responses client family with its own reasoning policy. Target carriers must be admitted before upstream calls.
- **Media:** media-job execution and Discord delivery are outside router metrics; their records below are dated evidence, not live gauges.

**Evidence dates:** live metric panels query Prometheus; the routing manifest and the capability surface were re-captured 2026-11-27 from release `20261126T212342Z-ceefc5bd6ea1a89e-e887392c` (manifest `e887392c…`), registry facts 2026-11-25; carrier/rerank/latency probes Nov11–16; media record Nov20. A 24-hour series showing an earlier process is not proof of the present release.
